newsitem.title: UK: No laws due to facilitate UK joining EMU - ministers.
newsitem.headline: No laws due to facilitate UK joining EMU - ministers.

text.p: Ministers on Thursday underscored the cabinet's adoption of a more "Euro-sceptic" stance toward monetary union by disclosing they had no plans for legislation in the first session of the next parliament to facilitate Britain's participation in a single European currency.

If past precedent is followed, the first session of the five-year parliament to be elected sometime in the next four months will run until mid-1998 -- just months before the January 1, 1999, starting date for economic and monetary union (EMU).

If it wanted to sign up to be ready for EMU, Britain would have to legislate in good time to make the Bank of England independent. In light of ministers' comments on Thursday, this would now be very difficult, although not an impossibility.
"It is definite legislation wouldn't be in the Queen's Speech and it is very unlikely that position would change during the (first) session," one minister said.

He was speaking after Prime Minister John Major said, following a 90-minute discussion in cabinet, that it was very unlikely though not impossible that Britain would sign up for EMU in the first wave in 1999.
